correctness.rationale: The general scalar reduction yields G(0)=0, G'(0)<0 from rho(M0)<1, G(x*)>0 and G(x) tending to negative infinity; hence two positive fixed points. For the displayed rational tuple, exact polynomial elimination has four simple isolated positive roots by four sign brackets and Descartes, of which precisely two satisfy 0<V<1. Exact derivative bounds establish one positive saddle and one positive sink; extinction is locally attracting. Independently runnable verify.py checks the polynomial identity, rational sign intervals, physical feasibility and hyperbolicity inequalities.

value.rationale: The question is naturally motivated by the local-extinction versus persistence dichotomy for source-sink dispersal. The general sufficient criterion shows how density-responsive allocation alone, with strict Beverton-Holt concavity and fixed total migration survival, creates two positive steady states below the low-density threshold. The all-positive-equilibrium count and stability types are exact, yield a robust open bistable region, and allow mathematically grounded intervention threshold reasoning. Not just a normalization check or an arbitrary polynomial.
